newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Dutch call for 5 pct 1998/99 cereals set-aside.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call for 5 pct 1998/99 cereals set-aside.

text.p: The Dutch EU Presidency on Tuesday urged the European Commission to rapidly propose that the compulsory set-aside rate for cereals should be maintained at five percent in the 1998/99 (July/June) marketing year.
But the suggestion, made in a compromise on the 1997/98 EU farm price package, was immediately rejected by the Commission which said that it was still too early to fix the rate.
"We first need all the data, it could turn out to be five percent but we can't be bound now," a Commission spokesman said.

The Dutch compromise, which will be discussed by EU farm ministers later on Tuesday, retains a proposal by EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to cut direct aid payments to cereals farmers by 1.4 billion Ecus so as to provide funds to help beef producers whose herds have been hit by mad cow disease.
However, on Monday nearly all EU countries strongly opposed the move saying it was unfair and unnecessary as there were spare funds in the 1997 budget.
Agreement on the farm price package is still a long way off, said one EU official.
